request.spec:
Add an audit viewer to the screen: a filter entry, a show button and a list of lines. With the
filter blank it lists every audit line of this sheet exactly as the file holds it, newest first.
With a name in the filter it lists only the lines about that person: those carrying name=<the
name> or person=<the name>, compared as names are compared (case and surrounding spaces ignored).
The viewer reads what the file holds; it is not a second record.

With a name in the filter it lists only the lines about that person: those carrying name=<the
name> or person=<the name>, compared as names are compared (case and surrounding spaces ignored).
The viewer reads what the file holds; it is not a second record.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text: That notice was the leftover watcher I set on the test run, and it can be ignored. The run had already finished before it ran out, with all 4 tests passing, so nothing has changed and the audit viewer is complete.
